notes.title: Access review is an owner attestation
notes.content: A campaign should show the person, role, system, entitlement, last use where available, manager and accountable application owner. IAM runs the campaign and evidence; it does not attest that another owner's grant remains necessary.

notes.title: Mover risk
notes.content: Role changes create more risk than simple joiners because old access can survive while new access is added. The record needs effective date, old and new manager, required-role delta, retained exceptions and confirmation that conflicting entitlements were removed.

notes.title: Privileged use review
notes.content: After emergency privileged access, verify who invoked it, the incident or care reason, approvals available at the time, commands or actions at an appropriate audit level, end time, credential rotation and owner review. Do not copy secrets into the evidence record.

notes.title: Contractor expiry
notes.content: Contractor access is tied to sponsor, contract scope, assignment and end date. A manager saying the person is useful does not extend the contract or privileged scope. Expiry should fail closed with a documented renewal path.

notes.title: Clinical break-glass boundary
notes.content: IAM can maintain the mechanism and audit trail but does not decide whether an individual clinical use was appropriate. Clinical, Privacy and Security owners review the event according to policy.

notes.title: Service-account ownership
notes.content: Every non-person account needs an accountable owner, purpose, credential custodian, rotation method, permitted systems and review date. A shared account with no owner is not made acceptable by frequent use.

notes.title: Standard access versus exception
notes.content: Standard role access can be automated only when the role definition and prerequisites are current. A request outside that model must remain visibly exceptional; IAM should not quietly widen the standard role to clear a queue.

notes.title: Coverage
notes.content: Routine provisioning and reviews are business-hours services. Urgent privileged access uses the security duty path and must be reviewed afterward. Elliot's approval rights do not imply personal twenty-four-hour availability.

notes.title: Cardiology check
notes.content: Elliot has a cardiology check after an abnormal screening result. No diagnosis has been confirmed; the appointment and test result must not be exposed through access-governance work.

notes.title: Identity-theft recovery
notes.content: Elliot froze his personal credit after a fraudulent account appeared and is disputing a £3,200 balance. This must not be confused with the privileged-access investigations he handles at work.

notes.title: Partner relocation discussion
notes.content: Elliot and his partner are privately considering a move next year. Nothing is decided, and the discussion should not be used to infer resignation risk or staffing plans.

notes.title: Access review — privileged exceptions
notes.content: The campaign exception file contains named dormant privileged accounts and credential-reset details. The CIO receives accountable-owner decisions and aggregate exceptions; credential material stays with authorised administrators.
